subject.title: gateway: cap/thumbnail inlined avatars in agents.list to bound response size

question: Should oversized configured avatars be omitted under a lower shared limit, or preserved through a projection-specific thumbnail or lazy reference?
rationale: The smallest candidate patch changes existing accepted avatar behavior, while preserving that behavior requires either image projection work or a broader gateway/client contract.

options.title: Projection Thumbnail
options.body: Keep the existing accepted source limit, produce a small visual thumbnail for gateway projections, and skip avatar resolution for metadata-only callers.

options.title: Lower Shared Limit
options.body: Land the 256 KiB shared cap and intentionally accept that larger existing avatars and uploads will no longer render.

options.title: Lazy Avatar Fetch
options.body: Add a reference and authenticated fetch surface, then migrate clients to lazy cached loading at greater protocol and client cost.

recommendation.title: Projection Thumbnail
recommendation.body: Keep the existing accepted source limit, produce a small visual thumbnail for gateway projections, and skip avatar resolution for metadata-only callers.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the shared limit and has the strongest recent ownership across the affected gateway and avatar surfaces.
